title: Three answers to one question
arc: The weekly business review shows three different numbers for active riders, and Asha wants one by Friday. The cause is not SQL; it is modelling: nobody agreed on the grain, a rider who changed city is counted twice, and history was overwritten. This week you design Meridian's first proper dimensional model: the four steps, keys, slowly changing dimensions, cumulative tables, and a graph for riders who bring in other riders.
previously: What is a grain, and why does every fact table need exactly one?
Which slowly changing dimension type keeps the past true?
Recall: what does an as-of join protect you from?
Why might a cumulative table beat recomputing history every day?
cliff: Three numbers for active riders. Which modelling step went missing?
A rider moved city and last month's revenue moved too. What was overwritten?
Revenue by tier: today's tier or the tier at trip time?
Next week a fare is charged twice and nobody notices. Which kind of fact hides it?

scenes.monday: Three dashboards, three answers to "how many active riders?". Asha wants one number by Friday and a reason the other two were wrong. Start with why model at all.
scenes.midweek: A rider moved from Pune to Goa, and last month's revenue moved with them. History was overwritten. Build a type 2 dimension so the past stays true.
scenes.friday: Join revenue to the rider's tier at the time of the trip, not today's. Then read the architect's lens: when a star is the right shape, and when it is not.
